computer-glow.description: Capability of the window that draws the glow at the edge of the display while computer control works (label `computer-glow`, built in src/commands/computer/surface.rs). It is empty on purpose: the page is one static file with a style sheet and no script, it lets every click through and takes no focus. It needs no permission, and it gets none.

default.description: Main-window capability. shell:allow-spawn is the only permission here that can start a process, and it is scoped to the two package runners external MCP servers are actually launched with (npx, uvx). Every general-purpose interpreter and container runtime was removed: node, deno, bun, python and py all take a one-shot eval flag (node -e, python -c), npm/pnpm/yarn run whatever a package.json in the cwd defines, and docker run -v /:/host hands out the whole disk. With those in the allow-list, any script-execution bug in the WebView (a PDF viewer, a markdown renderer, a dependency) was code execution on the user's machine rather than defacement inside the app. The three uvx entries are one program, not three: uv ships uvx.exe on Windows (docs.astral.sh/uv), which the bare name finds; uvx.cmd covers a shim a version manager or wrapper put on the PATH, the same way npx.cmd covers npm's shim; and $HOME/.local/bin/uvx.exe is the official installer's fixed location, for an LU that was started before the installer added that folder to the PATH. None of them takes an eval flag or starts anything but uvx.

mobile.description: Capability of the one webview a phone has (Android and iOS). No updater, because updates come through the store. No shell:allow-spawn, shell:allow-kill or shell:allow-stdin-write, because a phone starts no process. No window controls, because there is no window chrome. shell:allow-open stays for links that leave the app. lu-native:default is the native layer (share and save, device facts, lifecycle, the Remote transport, background downloads; mobile-docs/NATIVE-SCHICHT.md), deep-link:default the links that open the app (lu://oauth/callback, lu://remote).

onboarding.description: Capability of the first-launch window (label `onboarding`, built in src/onboarding_window.rs). Deliberately NOT the main-window capability: the wizard needs to move itself, minimise, close, listen for events and open a vendor's download page in the browser — nothing that spawns a process. The `shell:allow-spawn` entries of default.json exist for external MCP servers, which the wizard never starts; a window that runs before the user has set anything up gets the smallest surface that carries it.
